clue.text: It's sinful making love in a house in America

indicators.note: the first 'in' tells us the letter for love goes inside the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: a villa is a large house
taken as written
US is short for the United States of America
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone claims that making love in an American house is a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: the first is the container signal, the second is a plain piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wicked or criminal is sinful, in the manner of a stage villain.

clue.text: Stick in one-metre stake

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a pale is a pointed wooden stake, as in a fence

explanation.surface: A one-metre stake is being driven into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or run through with a point is to spear or stick something.

clue.text: Outsider, for ages second, much fancied to win

parts.note: for a long time, so long
a hot favourite is one strongly tipped to win

explanation.surface: A racing tip: a horse long considered an outsider is now much fancied to win.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is set at the racecourse, where an outsider and a favourite look like opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner given little chance of winning, at long odds, is an outsider.

clue.text: You must mix it in -and I do, too

indicators.note: to mix is to stir things together, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cook tells a helper to stir it in, and says they will do the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix' rearranges IT IN AND I DO; 'You must' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Also or as well, an extra amount on top of something already mentioned.

clue.text: Unusual dance card

parts.note: odd means unusual or strange
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An unusual card is handed round at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is old slang for an eccentric or amusing person, not a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric character, an amusing oddity, is informally called a card.

clue.text: Put up excellent performance

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting a word up means writing it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tops is slang for excellent, the very best

explanation.surface: A theatre company puts on an excellent show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like 'stage', but in a down clue it turns the word for excellent upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot or turn in a show, such as a comedy act, is a spot.

clue.text: The cheapest way to travel was always in a coach

indicators.note: in tells us the word for always sits inside the word for the coach

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Travelling by coach has always been the cheapest option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' is a link. E'ER is a poetic form of 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest class of passenger accommodation on a ship was called steerage.

clue.text: Plan put process out of kilter

indicators.note: out of kilter means out of order or askew, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A badly organised procedure has thrown a plan off course.
explanation.definitionFit: A document setting out a scheme or what an enterprise offers is a plan of sorts.

clue.text: Bill doesn't close back door

indicators.note: not closing means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a postern is a back or side gate of a castle

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill fails to shut the back door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is a name in the surface but means a printed notice; 'doesn't close' cuts the last letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice stuck up in public, a placard.

clue.text: Don's father overwhelmed by back taxes

indicators.note: one thing overwhelmed by another is engulfed in it, so the father goes inside
back means the word for taxes is written backwards

parts.note: drains means taxes or exhausts
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A university don's father is crushed by unpaid taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the taxes word round to SNIARD. Don is the Spanish title for a gentleman, not a university lecturer; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is the Spanish honorific for a gentleman, so a don is a man from Spain.

clue.text: The look of Cumberland

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang ... hook means look
the Duke of Cumberland was nicknamed the Butcher after Culloden, so the possessive means his

explanation.walkthrough: Cumberland was the Duke of Cumberland, called 'Butcher' after crushing the Jacobites at Culloden in 1746. Rhyming slang is Cockney London speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang turns a glance into a 'butcher's hook', and Cumberland was the Butcher.

clue.text: Engagement makes each side happy — to start with

indicators.note: to start with signals the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: An engagement leaves both families happy at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears are said to mesh when their teeth engage with each other.

clue.text: Girl heartlessly gossiping, distorting the facts

parts.note: miss is a word for a girl or young woman

indicators.note: without its heart means the middle letters of the word are removed

parts.note: tattling means gossiping or telling tales

explanation.surface: A girl is cruelly spreading gossip and twisting the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle pair TL out of TATTLING, leaving TATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a false account, saying something wrongly, distorts the facts.

clue.text: "Benighted!" I shall say, again and again

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall
to iterate is to say repeatedly

explanation.surface: Someone vows to keep calling another person benighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Benighted means in intellectual darkness, ignorant, as one unable to read is.

clue.text: Take steps to avoid going under

definitions.text: Take steps to avoid going under

parts.words: Take steps to avoid going under
parts.note: read literally, a swimmer moves the legs as if walking to stay afloat; figuratively, to keep a business from sinking

explanation.definitionFit: Keeping upright in deep water by pedalling the legs keeps a swimmer from sinking.

clue.text: Knits up woolly — it's out of this world

indicators.note: woolly means muddled or vague, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone knitting up a woolly jumper thinks it is out of this world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' looks like a knitted garment but scrambles KNITS UP. A jumper is a pullover sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: The first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviets in 1957, literally went into space.

clue.text: Not so affectionately, not so thoroughly, embracing relatives

annotationWithheld.why: Not so affectionately, not so thoroughly, embracing relatives (8): KIN in UNDLY, but no sense of 'not so thoroughly' gives UNDLY; the wordplay cannot be completed honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Not so affectionately, not so thoroughly, embracing relatives

clue.text: Part of group comprising members of FBI

indicators.note: comprising means containing, so the group holds the other piece

parts.note: a set is a group
G-men are US federal agents, members of the FBI

explanation.surface: A section of a group consists of FBI agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A section or portion of a whole is a part of it.

clue.text: The witching hour, when damsel wants a champion, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: a damsel is a maid and a champion is a knight, so maid and knight together

explanation.surface: A fairy tale: at the witching hour the damsel longs for a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants a' just joins MAID and KNIGHT, which spoken quickly sound like the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night is traditionally the hour when witches are abroad.

clue.text: Painstaking judge wearing old-fashioned headgear

indicators.note: someone wearing a hat is inside it, so the judge goes within the headgear

parts.note: a caul was a close-fitting cap or hairnet once worn by women
ref, short for referee, is a judge of play

explanation.surface: A meticulous judge sits in court in an antique cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking great pains means giving close attention, being meticulous.

clue.text: Start to control and cheat worker

parts.note: to take someone in is to deceive or cheat them
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A manager begins to take control and swindle an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: To take charge of something in order to manage it is to start controlling it.

clue.text: Appreciates having somewhere to live

definitions.meaning: dated slang for likes or understands
rented lodgings, a room or flat

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'digs' are rented rooms, often a student's lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for enjoying something, and British slang for lodgings rented as a home.

clue.text: Regard television mostly as provider of broad outlook

parts.note: to regard is to gaze at

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: Watching too much television narrows one's view of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the X from BOX; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A summerhouse built to command a wide view over a garden or landscape provides an outlook.

clue.text: 50% of score, about, in piece of writing for organ

parts.note: a score is twenty, and half of that is ten

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for about inside the story

parts.note: a tale is a story, a piece of writing
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone is composing music for the organ, half done.
explanation.walkthrough: Score and organ suggest music, but the score is twenty and the organ belongs to an octopus.
explanation.definitionFit: A long flexible limb of an octopus or squid, used for feeling and grasping, is a bodily organ.

clue.text: Penny in a state that's ecstatic by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: sent is slang for transported, carried away with delight

explanation.surface: Someone getting a penny is so pleased it sounds like rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a state' is one of the United States, where the penny coin is a hundredth of a dollar; 'in a state' also looks like agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest US coin, worth a hundredth of a dollar, is colloquially called a penny.

clue.text: Military clothing wears out

definitions.meaning: the plain working uniform soldiers wear
to wear out is to tire or exhaust

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' working dress, and a verb meaning tires or exhausts someone.

clue.text: Among colonels, one admiral stands out

indicators.note: among signals the answer is found within the following words

explanation.surface: In a group of colonels, one admiral is conspicuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands out' is a link telling us the admiral stands out within those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio, Lord Nelson, was the British admiral who won at Trafalgar in 1805.

clue.text: Changes in relation to religious freedom

indicators.note: changes in suggests alterations made to the following letters

explanation.surface: Reforms affecting religious liberty are being debated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerating faiths other than the established one allows freedom of worship.
